claims.claim: Choice screens typically present several logos or listed options and prompt users to select one.
For choice screens, a consequential selection of available options occurs before users see the screen.
Choice-screen operators select which candidates appear.
Choice-screen operators establish eligibility rules for listed candidates.
Choice-screen operators determine the ordering of listed candidates.
Choice-screen operators exclude options they regard as troublesome.
Human attention is scarce in choice-screen interactions.
Using interfaces imposes cognitive or practical work on users.
Preselecting an option on a choice screen influences user selection.
A preselected default requires fewer clicks than selecting an alternative.
A preselected default reduces how much users read.
A preselected default reduces user uncertainty.
Users under time pressure tend to accept a prearranged default rather than investigate the competitive implications of their options.
Default placement increases an option's distribution.
Increased distribution produces increased revenue for the selected provider.
Users can change the preselected option on the choice screens under discussion.
Choice-screen gatekeepers benefit from steering user traffic.
Choice-screen gatekeepers can define option categories and admission prices.
Choice-screen gatekeepers can require providers to complete technical integrations.
Choice-screen gatekeepers can reserve the most advantageous position for themselves or a favored option.
The gatekeeper controls described in the preceding discussion compound one another's effects.
A rival listed on a choice screen may be placed where users are unlikely to notice it.
An admitted rival may be subjected to burdens not captured by its nominal admission.
A visible rival may be prevented from communicating directly with customers.
Listing criteria can exclude providers as effectively as an outright ban.
Exclusion through listing criteria is less conspicuous and appears more favorable than an outright ban.
Choice screens controlled by gatekeepers are embedded in products with an existing user base.
Providing nominal choice can preserve the gatekeeper power that the measure is intended to reduce.
Offering limited visible choice can reduce criticism of a gatekeeper without changing its underlying power structure.
Technical debates about choice screens tend to focus excessively on the number of interface buttons.
Choice screens can produce beneficial outcomes.
Leaving rulemaking, contest, and delay powers with an incumbent causes presentation-focused regulation to preserve the incumbent's business model.
Choice screens display genuine market choice only when legal and engineering measures transfer relevant control beyond the screen.
